title: All jets of a constant rational section detect equality of morphisms
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], let $X$ be an integral separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $P\in X(k)$. Put $R=\mathcal O_{X,P}$, the stalk of the structure sheaf, and $\mathfrak m=\ker(R\to k)$. For $n\geq1$ write $X_n=\operatorname{Spec}(R/\mathfrak m^{n+1})$, with its canonical map to $X$; powers and quotients are as in [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient] and spectra as in [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Let $T$ be any finite-type $k$-scheme and $Z$ any separated $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Here separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let $E\subseteq T\times_kX$ be an open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion] containing $T\times_k\{P\}$; products mean scheme fibre products [def-pc-fibre-product]. Every $T\times_kX_n$ factors through $E$, since it has the same underlying support as $T\times_k\{P\}$. If two $k$-morphisms $f,g:E\to Z$ satisfy $f|_{T\times_kX_n}=g|_{T\times_kX_n}$ for every $n\geq1$, then $f=g$. The scheme $T$ may be nonreduced or disconnected; no smoothness of $X$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 00IQ (lemma-intersection-powers-ideal-module), especially (1) and its proof by local Krull intersection. Agent-formulated constant-family morphism-detection consequence, with its argument recorded in report.md; this geometric statement is not itself the Stacks lemma. It isolates the formal-detection input in Milne, Algebraic Groups, Proposition 8.9, printed p.150, for the rational-action argument of Proposition 8.25.

proof.text: Form the equalizer $q:Q\hookrightarrow E$ as the pullback of the closed diagonal $\Delta_{Z/k}:Z\to Z\times_k Z$ by $(f,g)$. The fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product] says that a map to $E$ factors through $Q$ exactly when its composites with $f,g$ agree. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change], $q$ is a closed immersion. Write $\mathcal I=\ker(\mathcal O_E\to q_*\mathcal O_Q)$. By the affine description in [def-weil-closed-immersion], on an affine $\operatorname{Spec}D\subset E$ the inverse image of $Q$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(D/L)$, where $L=\mathcal I(\operatorname{Spec}D)$. Our hypothesis says that every $T\times_k X_n\to E$ factors through $Q$. It suffices to prove $\mathcal I=0$, since the same affine description will then make $q$ an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 01QR (lemma-base-change-closed-immersion) and Tag 01QO (lemma-closed-immersion); equalizer formed by pulling back the separated diagonal.

proof.text: Fix an affine open $T_0=\operatorname{Spec}B$ of $T$. Choose an affine neighbourhood $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $P$ from a finite-type affine cover of $X$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Thus $A$ is a finite-type $k$-algebra and is a domain by [def-pc-integral-scheme]. Evaluation at $P$ gives $A\to k$ with kernel $\mathfrak p$ and $A/\mathfrak p=k$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], $R=A_{\mathfrak p}$ and $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak pR$. The field $k$ is Noetherian since its only ideals are $0,k$; hence $A$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], and $R$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-krull-intersection-jacobson] to the finite $R$-module $R$ and its maximal ideal, which is its Jacobson radical. This gives $\bigcap_{r\ge1}\mathfrak m^r=0$. The localization $A\to R$ is injective: a numerator killed by a denominator outside $\mathfrak p$ is zero in the domain $A$. Therefore $\bigcap_{r\ge1}\mathfrak p^r=0$ in $A$.

Put $C=B\otimes_k A$ and $J=\mathfrak p C$. The tensor-product and affine-spectrum universal properties [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product, def-weil-affine-spectrum], applied to [def-pc-fibre-product], identify $T_0\times_kU$ with $\operatorname{Spec}C$: a map to it is precisely a pair of compatible maps to the two affine factors. Choose a $k$-basis $(b_i)$ of the vector space $B$. Each element of $C$ has a unique finite expansion $\sum_i b_i\otimes a_i$; applying the coordinate linear functionals gives uniqueness. For each $r\ge1$, the ideal $J^r$ consists exactly of expansions whose coefficients lie in $\mathfrak p^r$ (expand products of generators, and conversely use $\mathfrak p^rC=J^r$). Thus $C/J^r=B\otimes_k(A/\mathfrak p^r)$, $C/J=B$, and $\bigcap_{r\ge1}J^r=0$ by step 2. Equivalently $C\to\prod_{n\ge1}C/J^{n+1}$ is injective; omitting the first power does not change the intersection.

source.place: Tag 00CX (lemma-tensor-product): elementary coefficient calculation from the tensor universal property; Tag 00IQ, elementary scalar-extension consequence.

proof.text: For $r\ge1$ the natural map $A/\mathfrak p^r\to R/\mathfrak m^r$ is an isomorphism. Indeed, if $s\notin\mathfrak p$, write $s=c(1-u)$ with $c=s(P)\in k^\times$ and $u\in\mathfrak p$; its inverse modulo $\mathfrak p^r$ is $c^{-1}\sum_{j=0}^{r-1}u^j$. Hence localizing $A/\mathfrak p^r$ outside $\mathfrak p$ changes nothing, by the universal property of localization [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization]. Together with step 3, this identifies $T_0\times_k X_n$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(C/J^{n+1})$, compatibly with its map to $T_0\times_kU$. The radical of $J^{n+1}$ equals that of $J$, so this map has the same underlying support as the constant section $\operatorname{Spec}(C/J)$. In particular it factors through the stated open $E$.

source.place: Elementary geometric-series inverse in a nilpotent quotient; Schemes Tag 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves), part (6).

proof.text: Let $F$ be the closed complement of $E\cap\operatorname{Spec}C$ in $\operatorname{Spec}C$, and write $F=V(K)$ for an ideal $K$ of $C$. This complement is disjoint from $V(J)$, because the entire constant section lies in $E$. Thus $V(K+J)=\varnothing$, whence $K+J=C$ (a proper ideal lies in a maximal ideal). Choose $h\in K$ with $1-h\in J$. Then $D(h)\subset E\cap\operatorname{Spec}C$ and $V(J)\subset D(h)$. The affine ring of $D(h)$ is $C_h$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime]. For every $r\ge1$, $h=1+j$ with $j\in J$ has inverse $\sum_{i=0}^{r-1}(-j)^i$ modulo $J^r$. Consequently the maps $C\to C/J^r$ extend uniquely to $C_h\to C/J^r$.

source.place: Tag 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves), part (3); elementary Zariski closed-set and finite geometric-series calculations.

proof.text: The combined homomorphism $C_h\to\prod_{n\ge1}C/J^{n+1}$ is injective. To see this, write an element as $c/h^e$. If every image is zero, then multiplication by the unit $h^e$ in each quotient shows $c\in J^{n+1}$ for every $n\ge1$, so $c=0$ by step 3. The closed subscheme $Q\times_E D(h)$ is $\operatorname{Spec}(C_h/L_h)$ for an ideal $L_h$ by [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Each $\operatorname{Spec}(C/J^{n+1})$ factors through it by steps 1, 4, and 5; hence $L_h$ is killed by every displayed quotient map. Injectivity forces $L_h=0$. Thus $Q$ equals $E$ over $D(h)$, as schemes, and $\mathcal I|_{D(h)}=0$.

source.place: Elementary fraction calculation using the separated filtration from Tag 00IQ; Morphisms Tag 01QO (lemma-closed-immersion), affine closed-subscheme description.

proof.text: Restriction of regular functions from $T_0\times_k X$ to $D(h)$ is injective on every open subset. First $h$ is a non-zero-divisor on $C$: if $hc=0$, its unit images modulo all $J^{n+1}$ give $c=0$ by step 3. This remains true in $C_s$ for every $s\in C$: an equation $hc/s^e=0$ implies $s^N hc=0$ in $C$ for some $N$, and cancellation of $h$ gives $c/s^e=0$. Thus $C_s\to C_{sh}$ is injective, proving the assertion inside $T_0\times_kU$ on its basis of principal opens [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime]. Next, for any nonempty affine $V=\operatorname{Spec}A'$ of $X$, integrality [def-pc-integral-scheme] implies $U\cap V\ne\varnothing$, and it contains a nonempty principal open $D(a)$ of $V$, with $0\ne a\in A'$. Multiplication by $a$ is injective on the domain $A'$ and therefore on $B\otimes_k A'$ coefficient by coefficient in the same $k$-basis of $B$ used in step 3. The preceding localization argument gives injective restrictions on every principal open of $T_0\times_kV$ to its intersection with $T_0\times_kD(a)$. Since $D(a)\subset U\cap V$, any regular function vanishing on the intersection with $T_0\times_kU$ is zero. Covering by these principal opens proves injectivity on every open, by the sheaf uniqueness axiom. Composing the two injective restrictions proves the claimed injection to $D(h)$.

source.place: Tag 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves), part (3); elementary coefficient and localized-fraction arguments, expanding the schematic-density argument of Morphisms lemma-flat-morphism-scheme-theoretically-dense-open.

proof.text: Apply step 7 to open subsets of $E_0=E\cap(T_0\times_kX)$. Every section of $\mathcal I|_{E_0}$ is a regular function whose restriction to $D(h)$ is zero by step 6, so it is zero. Hence $\mathcal I|_{E_0}=0$. The affine opens $T_0$ cover $T$, so these $E_0$ cover $E$, and sheaf uniqueness gives $\mathcal I=0$. Step 1 now identifies $Q$ with $E$ and gives $f=g$. If $T$ is empty the conclusion is immediate; the argument treats disconnected or nonreduced affine $T_0$ because it used only that its coordinate ring $B$ is a $k$-vector space. No regularity or smoothness of $R$ was used.
